# Load packages

```{r}
# Note: In case of dependency issues, Run: update.packages(ask = FALSE, checkBuilt = TRUE)
# install.packages('rlang')

#' Ensure specified packages are installed and loaded.
#'
#' Checks if packages are installed, installs missing ones,
#' then attempts to load all specified packages. Uses '=' for assignment.
#'
#' @param pkg_list A character vector of package names.
#' @return Invisibly returns a named logical vector indicating load success for each package.
load_packages = function(pkg_list) {
  
  # Ensure package list is unique
  pkg_list = unique(pkg_list)
  
  # Identify installed packages
  installed_pkgs = rownames(installed.packages())
  
  # Find packages that need installation
  missing_pkgs = pkg_list[!pkg_list %in% installed_pkgs]
  
  # Install missing packages if any exist
  if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
    message("Installing missing packages: ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "))
    tryCatch({
      install.packages(missing_pkgs, dependencies = TRUE)
      # Update the list of known installed packages *after* installation attempt
      installed_pkgs = rownames(installed.packages()) 
    }, error = function(e) {
      warning("Installation failed for some packages: ", conditionMessage(e))
    })
  }
  
  message("Loading required packages...")
  # Attempt to load all packages in the list
  load_status = sapply(pkg_list, function(pkg) {
    # Check if it's actually installed before trying to load
    if (pkg %in% installed_pkgs) {
      # Use require() as it returns TRUE/FALSE, suitable for sapply
      # suppressPackageStartupMessages keeps the console cleaner
      loaded = suppressPackageStartupMessages(
        require(pkg, character.only = TRUE, quietly = TRUE)
      )
      if (!loaded) {
        warning("Failed to load package: ", pkg)
      }
      return(loaded)
    } else {
      # If it's not in installed_pkgs (even after install attempt)
      warning("Package '", pkg, "' not found or failed to install. Cannot load.")
      return(FALSE)
    }
  })
  
  # Report final status
  if (all(load_status)) {
    message("All required packages loaded successfully.")
  } else {
    failed_pkgs = names(load_status[!load_status])
    warning("Failed to load or install the following packages: ",
            paste(failed_pkgs, collapse = ", "), ".")
  }
  
  # Return the status invisibly (useful for checking programmatically if needed)
  invisible(load_status)
}


# --- Usage ---
```

# Process exposure windows

```{r}
count_unique_subjects = function(exposure_data) {
  # Create a data frame to store results
  results = data.frame(
    window = character(),
    start_date = as.Date(character()),
    end_date = as.Date(character()),
    duration = numeric(),
    n_subjects = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Loop through all time windows
  for (window_name in names(exposure_data)) {
    window = exposure_data[[window_name]]
    
    # Count unique person_ids
    n_unique = length(unique(window$data$person_id))
    
    # Add to results
    results = rbind(results, data.frame(
      window = window_name,
      start_date = window$start_date,
      end_date = window$end_date,
      duration = window$duration,
      n_subjects = n_unique,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))
  }
  
  # Order by start date and duration
  results = results[order(results$start_date, results$duration), ]
  
  return(results)
}

# Usage
subject_counts = count_unique_subjects(combined_exposure_data_clean)


# Step 1: Process ALL exposure windows from combined_exposure_data
process_all_exposure_windows = function(combined_exposure_data_clean) {
  # Create empty list to store processed windows
  all_windows = list()
  column_map_list = list()
  
  # Process each exposure window
  for(window_name in names(combined_exposure_data_clean)) {
    window_data = combined_exposure_data_clean[[window_name]]
    
    # Extract window metadata
    start_date = format(window_data$start_date, "%Y%m%d")
    duration = window_data$duration
    
    if(FALSE){ ### Updated to match original window names
    suffix = paste0("_", start_date, "_", duration, "d")
    }
    
    # Get suffix
    suffix_old = paste0("_", start_date, "_", duration, "d")
    suffix_new = paste0("_", sub("_dur\\d+$", "", window_name))
    
    
    # Process policy columns
    window_df = window_data$data %>%
      select(person_id, 
             C1M_School_closing,
             C2M_Workplace_closing,
             C3M_Cancel_public_events,
             C4M_Restrictions_on_gatherings,
             C5M_Close_public_transport,
             C6M_Stay_at_home_requirements,
             C7M_Restrictions_on_internal_movement) %>%
      # Modified rename to match the expected pattern in policy_impact_regression
      rename_with(~ paste0(str_extract(., "^C[1-7]M"), suffix_old), -person_id)
    
    old_names = names(window_df)[names(window_df) != "person_id"]
    new_names = str_replace(string = old_names, pattern = suffix_old, replacement = suffix_new)
    
    column_map_list[[window_name]] = data.frame(
      old_name = old_names,
      new_name = new_names,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
      
    all_windows[[window_name]] = window_df
  }
    
    merged_df = reduce(all_windows, full_join, by = "person_id")
    column_map_df = bind_rows(column_map_list)
    
    return(list(
      all_exposure_data = merged_df,
      column_map = column_map_df
    ))
  
}

# Process all 120 exposure windows
processed = process_all_exposure_windows(combined_exposure_data_clean)
all_exposure_data = processed$all_exposure_data
column_map = processed$column_map

```

# Cluster grouping for train test split
```{r}
# Create stratified train/test split based on GAD-7 outcome (50/50)
# Create GAD-7 quartile bins
gad_quantiles = quantile(cope_auo_full$gad_score_july, probs = 0:3/3, na.rm = TRUE)
print(gad_quantiles) # 0, 1, 5, 21

# Create GAD-7 tertile bins using quantile values (specified above)
cope_auo_full$gad_category = cut(cope_auo_full$gad_score_july,
                                 breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 21),
                                 labels = c("None", "Minimal", "Mild_Severe"),
                                 include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)

cope_auo_full$gad_category = cut(cope_auo_full$gad_score_july,
                                 breaks = c(0, 5, 15, 21),
                                 labels = c("Minimal", "Mild", "Moderate_Severe"),
                                 include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)

# Check for missing values in gad_category after cut()
cat("Checking for missing values in gad_category after cut() function:\n")
gad_category_table = table(cope_auo_full$gad_category, useNA = "ifany")
print(gad_category_table)

# Check if there are any missing values
missing_count = sum(is.na(cope_auo_full$gad_category))
cat("Number of missing values in gad_category:", missing_count, "\n")

if(missing_count > 0) {
  warning("Missing values detected in gad_category. Investigating...")
  # Show which original GAD scores led to missing categories
  missing_gad_scores = cope_auo_full$gad_score_july[is.na(cope_auo_full$gad_category)]
  cat("Original GAD scores that resulted in missing categories:\n")
  print(summary(missing_gad_scores))
} else {
  cat("✓ No missing values in gad_category after cut() function\n")
}
cat("\n")

# Identify states with sufficient sample sizes for individual stratification
large_states = cope_auo_full %>%
  count(RegionName) %>%
  filter(n >= 400) %>%  # Conservative threshold for adequate severe cases
  pull(RegionName)


# Create grouping across US regions 
cope_auo_full$region_grouped = case_when(
  cope_auo_full$RegionName %in% large_states ~ as.character(cope_auo_full$RegionName),
  cope_auo_full$RegionName %in% c("Maine", "New Hampshire", "Vermont", "Rhode Island", "Connecticut") ~ "New_England",
  cope_auo_full$RegionName %in% c("Delaware", "Maryland", "Virginia", "West Virginia", "Kentucky", "Tennessee") ~ "Mid_Atlantic_South",
  cope_auo_full$RegionName %in% c("North Carolina", "South Carolina", "Georgia", "Alabama", "Mississippi", "Louisiana", "Arkansas") ~ "Southeast",
  cope_auo_full$RegionName %in% c("Indiana", "Missouri", "Iowa", "Kansas", "Nebraska", "North Dakota", "South Dakota") ~ "Midwest_Plains",
  cope_auo_full$RegionName %in% c("Montana", "Wyoming", "Colorado", "Utah", "Idaho", "Nevada", "New Mexico") ~ "Mountain_West",
  cope_auo_full$RegionName %in% c("Oregon", "Washington", "Alaska", "Hawaii") ~ "Pacific_Northwest",
  TRUE ~ "Other_States"
)

# Create combined stratification variable
cope_auo_full$strata_var = paste(cope_auo_full$region_grouped, cope_auo_full$gad_category, sep = "_")

# Check for any remaining small strata
strata_counts = table(cope_auo_full$strata_var)
small_strata = strata_counts[strata_counts < 20]
if(length(small_strata) > 0) {
  print("Remaining small strata:")
  print(small_strata)
}
```

# Initial Split

```{r}
# The initial_split() function from rsample failed to execute stratified sampling despite multiple attempts to consolidate regional groupings and adjust the pool parameter. 
# The function's default behavior requires a minimum threshold of observations within each stratum that appears to be overly conservative for our purposes.
# This issue persisted, even with pool = 0.1, which should allow strata representing as little as 10% of the dataset.
#
# This manual implementation addresses these limitations by ensuring that each combination of geographic region (region_grouped) and GAD-7 category (gad_category) maintains 
# proportional representation across training and testing datasets. 
# The floor() function determines training set sizes within  ach stratum by rounding down to the nearest integer, which prevents fractional allocations 
# This also ensures that smaller strata contribute at least some observations to both datasets when possible.
#
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(42)

# Load required libraries (add purrr for map_dfr function)
library(purrr)

# Manual stratified sampling split
stratified_data = cope_auo_full %>%
  
  # Group observations by geographic region and anxiety severity level
  group_by(region_grouped, gad_category) %>%
  
  # Randomly shuffle observations within each combination of region and GAD category
  # This prevents any bias from the ordering of rows in the original data 
  mutate(random_order = runif(n())) %>%
  arrange(random_order) %>%
  
  # Determine how many observations from each stratum go to training vs testing
  # Using floor ensures we get whole numbers and maintain the 50/50 split intention
  mutate(
    stratum_size = n(),
    train_size = floor(stratum_size * 0.50),
    train_flag = row_number() <= train_size
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Creating training and testing datasets
train_data = stratified_data %>% filter(train_flag == TRUE)
test_data = stratified_data %>% filter(train_flag == FALSE)

# STORE PRE-RERANDOMIZATION DATASETS FOR COMPARISON
train_data_pre_rerand = train_data
test_data_pre_rerand = test_data

# Display overall split sizes
cat("Total observations:", nrow(cope_auo_full), "\n")
cat("Training set:", nrow(train_data), "\n") 
cat("Testing set:", nrow(test_data), "\n")
cat("Training proportion:", round(nrow(train_data) / nrow(cope_auo_full), 3), "\n")
cat("Testing proportion:", round(nrow(test_data) / nrow(cope_auo_full), 3), "\n")

```

# Comparison: manual vs tidymodels approach

```{r}

# Adding tidymodels approach for comparison
set.seed(42)
data_split_tidymodels = initial_split(cope_auo_full, prop = 0.50, strata = "strata_var", pool = 0.05)
train_data_tidymodels = training(data_split_tidymodels)
test_data_tidymodels = testing(data_split_tidymodels)

# Comparing overall split sizes
cat("Manual Method - Training:", nrow(train_data), "Testing:", nrow(test_data), "\n")
cat("Tidymodels Method - Training:", nrow(train_data_tidymodels), "Testing:", nrow(test_data_tidymodels), "\n\n")
```

```{r}
# Verify stratification across regions - comparing both methods
# Counts and proportions are kept separate for better readability
verifying_state_stratification_counts = bind_rows(
  # Manual method results
  train_data %>%
    count(region_grouped) %>%
    mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "training"),
  test_data %>%
    count(region_grouped) %>%
    mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "testing"),
  # Tidymodels method results
  train_data_tidymodels %>%
    count(region_grouped) %>%
    mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "training"),
  test_data_tidymodels %>%
    count(region_grouped) %>%
    mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "testing")
) %>%
  select(region_grouped, method, dataset, n) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(method, dataset), values_from = n, names_sep = "_")

verifying_state_stratification_proportions = bind_rows(
  # Manual method results
  train_data %>%
    count(region_grouped) %>%
    mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "training", proportion = n / sum(n)),
  test_data %>%
    count(region_grouped) %>%
    mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "testing", proportion = n / sum(n)),
  # Tidymodels method results
  train_data_tidymodels %>%
    count(region_grouped) %>%
    mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "training", proportion = n / sum(n)),
  test_data_tidymodels %>%
    count(region_grouped) %>%
    mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "testing", proportion = n / sum(n))
) %>%
  select(region_grouped, method, dataset, proportion) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(method, dataset), values_from = proportion, names_sep = "_")
```

# Visualization

```{r}
# Visualization for state counts

# Reshape data for ggplot (focusing on manual splits)
state_stratification_long = verifying_state_stratification_counts %>%
  select(region_grouped, manual_training, manual_testing) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(manual_training, manual_testing),
               names_to = "split_type",
               values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(
    split_type = case_when(
      split_type == "manual_training" ~ "Training",
      split_type == "manual_testing" ~ "Testing"
    ),
    split_type = factor(split_type, levels = c("Training", "Testing"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(count))

# Horizontal plot to reduce clutter
state_horizontal_plot = ggplot(state_stratification_long,
                                aes(x = count,
                                    y = reorder(region_grouped, count),
                                    fill = count)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = count),
            hjust = -0.1,
            size = 3,
            fontface = "bold") +
  facet_wrap(~ split_type, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#E6E6FA", high = "#4B0082",
                      name = "Count") +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "State Stratification Counts - Stratified Training/Testing Split",
       y = "State/Region",

  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines")) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15)))

# Print summary statistics
cat("Stratified Training/Testing Split Summary:\n")
summary_stats = state_stratification_long %>%
  group_by(split_type) %>%
  summarise(
    min_count = min(count),
```

# Rerandomization functions

```{r}
#' Create a single stratified train/test split
#'
#' This function creates a train/test split using either manual stratified sampling
#' or tidymodels approach. The manual method stratifies by region_grouped and gad_category,
#' randomly ordering observations within each stratum and allocating 50% to training.
#'
#' @param data The full dataset to split
#' @param seed_value Seed for reproducible randomization
#' @param method Either "manual" for custom stratified sampling or "tidymodels" for rsample approach
#' @return List containing train_data, test_data, and seed value
create_stratified_split = function(data, seed_value, method = "manual") {
  set.seed(seed_value)

  if(method == "manual") {
    # Manual stratified sampling: stratify by region and GAD category
    stratified_data = data %>%
      group_by(region_grouped, gad_category) %>%
      mutate(random_order = runif(n())) %>%  # Random ordering within strata
      arrange(random_order) %>%
      mutate(
        stratum_size = n(),
        train_size = floor(stratum_size * 0.50),  # 50% to training, rounded down
        train_flag = row_number() <= train_size
      ) %>%
      ungroup()

    train_data = stratified_data %>% filter(train_flag == TRUE)
    test_data = stratified_data %>% filter(train_flag == FALSE)

  } else if(method == "tidymodels") {
    # Using tidymodels initial_split with stratification
    data_split = initial_split(data, prop = 0.50, strata = "strata_var", pool = 0.05)
    train_data = training(data_split)
    test_data = testing(data_split)
  }

  return(list(train = train_data, test = test_data, seed = seed_value))
}


#' Calculate balance score using logistic regression AUC
#'
#' This function measures how well covariates can predict whether an observation
#' is in the training or test set. Lower AUC (closer to 0.5) indicates better
#' balance, as covariates cannot distinguish between train/test groups.
#' This is the key metric for rerandomization selection.
#'
#' @param train_data Training dataset
#' @param test_data Test dataset
#' @param covariates Vector of covariate names to include in balance model
#' @return List with AUC value and diagnostic information
calculate_balance_auc = function(train_data, test_data, covariates) {
  # Combine datasets with group indicator (0=train, 1=test)
  combined_data = bind_rows(
    train_data %>% select(all_of(covariates)) %>% mutate(group = 0),
    test_data %>% select(all_of(covariates)) %>% mutate(group = 1)
  )

  # Remove rows with any missing values in covariates
  complete_data = combined_data %>%
    select(all_of(c(covariates, "group"))) %>%
    na.omit()

  if(nrow(complete_data) < 50) {
    warning("Insufficient complete observations for AUC calculation")
    return(list(auc = NA, n_complete = nrow(complete_data)))
  }

  # Convert categorical variables to factors for modeling
  for(covar in covariates) {
    if(covar %in% names(complete_data)) {
      if(is.character(complete_data[[covar]]) || is.factor(complete_data[[covar]])) {
        complete_data[[covar]] = factor(complete_data[[covar]])
      }
    }
  }

  # Build formula - include all available covariates
  # No restriction on categorical levels since our max is 9 levels
  formula_parts = character(0)
  for(covar in covariates) {
    if(covar %in% names(complete_data)) {
      formula_parts = c(formula_parts, covar)
    }
  }

  if(length(formula_parts) == 0) {
    warning("No suitable covariates for balance regression")
    return(list(auc = NA, n_complete = nrow(complete_data)))
  }

  # Create logistic regression formula: group ~ all_covariates
  formula_str = paste("group ~", paste(formula_parts, collapse = " + "))

  # Fit logistic regression predicting train/test assignment from covariates
  tryCatch({
    balance_model = glm(as.formula(formula_str),
                        data = complete_data,
                        family = binomial())

    # Get predicted probabilities of being in test set
    predictions = predict(balance_model, type = "response")

    # Calculate AUC: How well can covariates predict train/test assignment?
    # AUC near 0.5 = poor prediction = good balance
    # AUC near 1.0 = excellent prediction = poor balance
    auc_result = pROC::auc(complete_data$group, predictions, quiet = TRUE)

    return(list(
      auc = as.numeric(auc_result),
      n_complete = nrow(complete_data),
      n_predictors = length(formula_parts),
      model_converged = balance_model$converged
    ))

  }, error = function(e) {
    warning(paste("Error in balance regression:", e$message))
    return(list(auc = NA, n_complete = nrow(complete_data)))
  })
}


#' Perform rerandomization to find optimal train/test split
#'
#' This function generates multiple candidate train/test splits and selects
#' the one with the best covariate balance (lowest AUC). This addresses
#' the concern that random chance imbalance could drive differences in
#' policy effect estimates between training and test sets.
#'
#' HOW AUC MEASURES BALANCE:
#' 1. Combine train/test data with group indicator (0=train, 1=test)
#' 2. Run logistic regression: group ~ all_covariates
#' 3. AUC measures how well covariates predict group membership
#' 4. AUC ~ 0.5 = covariates can't predict groups = GOOD balance
#' 5. AUC ~ 1.0 = covariates perfectly predict groups = BAD balance
#' 6. Select split with LOWEST AUC = best balance
#'
#' @param data Full dataset to split
#' @param n_randomizations Number of candidate splits to generate (10-50 would be recommended, setting default of 10)
#' @param method Splitting method ("manual" or "tidymodels")
#' @return List containing best split, all results, and diagnostics
perform_rerandomization = function(data, n_randomizations = 10, method = "manual") {

  set.seed(505)
  cat("Performing rerandomization with", n_randomizations, "random splits...\n")
  cat("Goal: Find split where covariates CANNOT predict train vs test assignment\n")

  # Initialize tracking variables (much smaller memory footprint than storing all splits)
  best_auc = Inf                           # Track best AUC score found so far
  best_seed = NULL                         # Track seed that produced best AUC
  all_aucs = numeric(n_randomizations)     # Store only AUC values (not full datasets)
  all_seeds = numeric(n_randomizations)    # Store corresponding seeds for analysis

  # Progress tracking with error handling
  pb = txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = n_randomizations, style = 3)

  # MAIN LOOP: Generate and evaluate each candidate split
  for(i in 1:n_randomizations) {

    # Update progress bar
    setTxtProgressBar(pb, i)

    # Generate random seed for this iteration
    seed_i = sample(1:100000, 1)
    all_seeds[i] = seed_i  # Store seed for potential analysis

    tryCatch({
      # STEP 1: Create stratified split using specified method
      # This maintains stratification by region_grouped and gad_category
      # but randomizes assignment within each stratum
      split_result = create_stratified_split(data, seed_i, method)

      # STEP 2: Measure balance quality using AUC approach
      # This tests how well covariates can distinguish train from test observations
      auc_result = calculate_balance_auc(
        split_result$train,    # Training observations
        split_result$test,     # Test observations
        existing_covariates    # Covariates to test for balance
      )

      # STEP 3: Store only the AUC score (tiny memory footprint vs full datasets)
      all_aucs[i] = auc_result$auc

      # STEP 4: Update best split tracker if this one is better (lower AUC)
      if(!is.na(auc_result$auc) && auc_result$auc < best_auc) {
        best_auc = auc_result$auc
        best_seed = seed_i
      }

      # STEP 5: Immediately removing stored large objects (to avoid crashing)
      rm(split_result, auc_result)
      gc()  # Force garbage collection to free memory immediately

    }, error = function(e) {
      # Pasting a warning message if an error occurred in the randomization
      warning(paste("Error in randomization", i, ":", e$message))
      all_aucs[i] = NA
    })

    # Memory management for large datasets
    if(i %% 5 == 0) {
      gc()  # Additional cleanup every 5 iterations
    }
  }

  close(pb)
  cat("\n")  # New line after progress bar

  # Report results and improvement achieved
  cat("=== Rerandomization results ===\n")
  cat("Number of valid randomizations:", sum(!is.na(all_aucs)), "\n")

  # Show AUC range
  auc_range = range(all_aucs, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("AUC range:", round(auc_range[1], 4), "to", round(auc_range[2], 4), "\n")
  auc_improvement = round((auc_range[2] - auc_range[1]) / auc_range[2] * 100, 1)
  cat("AUC improvement from rerandomization:", auc_improvement, "%\n")

  cat("Best AUC (lower = better balance):", round(best_auc, 4), "\n")
  cat("Best seed:", best_seed, "\n\n")

  # FINAL STEP: Recreate only the best split for subsequent analysis
  # This saves memory compared to keeping all splits in memory throughout
  cat("Recreating optimal split...\n")
  final_split = create_stratified_split(data, best_seed, method)

  # Return comprehensive results
  return(list(
    best_split = final_split,              # The selected train/test split
    best_auc = best_auc,                   # AUC of the selected split
    best_seed = best_seed,                 # Seed that produced the best split
    all_aucs = all_aucs,                   # AUC scores for all splits tested
    all_seeds = all_seeds,                 # Seeds for all splits tested
    auc_improvement = auc_improvement      # Percentage improvement from rerandomization
  ))
}
```

# Balance stats

```{r}
#' Calculate balance statistics for train/test split
#'
#' This function computes standardized mean differences (SMD), variance ratios,
#' and distributional tests for all covariates. For continuous/binary variables,
#' it calculates SMD and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests. For categorical variables,
#' it performs chi-square tests and calculates Cramer's V effect sizes.
#'
#' @param train_data Training dataset
#' @param test_data Test dataset
#' @param covariates Vector of covariate names to assess
#' @return List with balance_results tibble and categorical_results list
calculate_balance = function(train_data, test_data, covariates) {
  balance_results = tibble()
  categorical_results = list()

  for(var in covariates) {
    # Skip variables not present in both datasets
    if(!var %in% names(train_data) || !var %in% names(test_data)) {
      next
    }

    train_var = train_data[[var]]
    test_var = test_data[[var]]

    # Remove missing values for statistical calculations
    train_complete = train_var[!is.na(train_var)]
    test_complete = test_var[!is.na(test_var)]

    if(length(train_complete) == 0 || length(test_complete) == 0) {
      next
    }

    if(is.numeric(train_var) && is.numeric(test_var)) {
      # CONTINUOUS VARIABLE ANALYSIS
      mean_train = mean(train_complete)
      mean_test = mean(test_complete)
      var_train = var(train_complete)
      var_test = var(test_complete)

      # Calculate pooled standard deviation for SMD
      pooled_sd = sqrt((var_train + var_test) / 2)

      # Standardized Mean Difference: effect size independent of units
      smd = (mean_train - mean_test) / pooled_sd

      # Variance ratio: should be close to 1 for good balance
      variance_ratio = var_train / var_test

      # Kolmogorov-Smirnov test: compares full distributions
      # Note: Warnings about ties are normal for discrete/integer data
      ks_test = suppressWarnings(ks.test(train_complete, test_complete))

      balance_results = bind_rows(balance_results, tibble(
        variable = var,
        type = "continuous",
        mean_train = mean_train,
        mean_test = mean_test,
        var_train = var_train,
        var_test = var_test,
        smd = smd,
        abs_smd = abs(smd),
        variance_ratio = variance_ratio,
        ks_statistic = ks_test$statistic,
        ks_p_value = ks_test$p.value,
        n_train = length(train_complete),
        n_test = length(test_complete)
      ))

    } else {
      # CATEGORICAL VARIABLE ANALYSIS
      train_factor = factor(train_complete)
      test_factor = factor(test_complete)

      # Ensure both factors have same levels for comparison
      all_levels = unique(c(levels(train_factor), levels(test_factor)))
      train_factor = factor(train_complete, levels = all_levels)
      test_factor = factor(test_complete, levels = all_levels)

      if(length(all_levels) == 2) {
        # BINARY CATEGORICAL: Calculate SMD for proportions
        prop_train = mean(train_factor == all_levels[1])
        prop_test = mean(test_factor == all_levels[1])

        # SMD for binary variables using pooled proportion
        pooled_prop = (prop_train + prop_test) / 2
        pooled_se = sqrt(pooled_prop * (1 - pooled_prop))
        smd = (prop_train - prop_test) / pooled_se

        balance_results = bind_rows(balance_results, tibble(
          variable = var,
          type = "binary",
          mean_train = prop_train,
          mean_test = prop_test,
          var_train = NA,
          var_test = NA,
          smd = smd,
          abs_smd = abs(smd),
          variance_ratio = NA,
          ks_statistic = NA,
          ks_p_value = NA,
          n_train = length(train_complete),
          n_test = length(test_complete)
        ))
      } else {
        # MULTI-LEVEL CATEGORICAL: Use chi-square test and Cramer's V
        combined_data = data.frame(
          group = factor(c(rep("train", length(train_complete)),
                           rep("test", length(test_complete)))),
          variable = factor(c(train_complete, test_complete), levels = all_levels)
        )

        tryCatch({
          # Chi-square test for independence of variable and group
          chi_test = chisq.test(table(combined_data$variable, combined_data$group))

          # Cramer's V: effect size measure for categorical associations
          n = nrow(combined_data)
          cramers_v = sqrt(chi_test$statistic / (n * (min(length(all_levels), 2) - 1)))

          categorical_results[[var]] = list(
            variable = var,
            type = "categorical",
            n_levels = length(all_levels),
            chi_square = chi_test$statistic,
            chi_p_value = chi_test$p.value,
            cramers_v = as.numeric(cramers_v),
            train_table = table(train_factor),
            test_table = table(test_factor),
            n_train = length(train_complete),
            n_test = length(test_complete)
          )
        }, error = function(e) {
          categorical_results[[var]] = list(
            variable = var,
            type = "categorical_error",
            error = e$message,
            n_train = length(train_complete),
            n_test = length(test_complete)
          )
        })

        # Add placeholder row in main results for categorical variables
        balance_results = bind_rows(balance_results, tibble(
          variable = var,
          type = "categorical",
          mean_train = NA,
          mean_test = NA,
          var_train = NA,
          var_test = NA,
          smd = NA,
          abs_smd = NA,
          variance_ratio = NA,
          ks_statistic = NA,
          ks_p_value = NA,
          n_train = length(train_complete),
          n_test = length(test_complete)
        ))
      }
    }
  }

  return(list(
    balance_results = balance_results,
    categorical_results = categorical_results
  ))
}
```

## Balance Plot functions

```{r}
#' Create separate balance plots for continuous/binary vs categorical variables
#'
#' @param balance_results Balance results from calculate_balance()
#' @param categorical_results Categorical balance results from calculate_balance()
#' @param pre_randomization Logical. If TRUE, changes title to indicate pre-rerandomization results
#' @param smd_limits Numeric vector of length 2 specifying y-axis limits for SMD plot. Default c(-0.1, 0.1)
#' @return List containing two ggplot objects: continuous_plot and categorical_plot
create_balance_plots = function(balance_results, categorical_results, pre_randomization = FALSE, smd_limits = c(-0.1, 0.1)) {

  # Set title prefix based on pre_randomization parameter
  title_prefix = if(pre_randomization) {
    "Before Rerandomization:"
  } else {
    "After Rerandomization:"
  }

  # PLOT 1: CONTINUOUS AND BINARY VARIABLES (using SMD)
  continuous_results = balance_results %>%
    filter(type %in% c("continuous", "binary")) %>%
    select(variable, smd) %>%
    mutate(
      variable_type = case_when(
        variable %in% c("sex", "birthplace") ~ "Binary",
        TRUE ~ "Continuous"
      ),
      abs_smd = abs(smd),
      balance_quality = case_when(
        abs_smd <= 0.05 ~ "Excellent (<=0.05)",
        abs_smd <= 0.1 ~ "Good (0.05-0.1)",
        TRUE ~ "Moderate (>0.1)"
      ),
      balance_quality = factor(balance_quality,
                               levels = c("Excellent (<=0.05)", "Good (0.05-0.1)",
                                          "Moderate (>0.1)"))
    )

  continuous_plot = ggplot(continuous_results, aes(x = factor(variable, levels = rev(all_vars_alphabetical)), y = smd)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-0.2, -0.1, -0.05, 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2),
               color = c("red", "orange", "darkgreen", "black", "darkgreen", "orange", "red"),
               linetype = c("dashed", "dashed", "dashed", "solid", "dashed", "dashed", "dashed"),
               alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_point(aes(color = balance_quality, shape = variable_type), size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Excellent (<=0.05)" = "#006400",
                                  "Good (0.05-0.1)" = "#2E8B57",
                                  "Moderate (>0.1)" = "#FF8C00")) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("Continuous" = 16, "Binary" = 17)) +
    coord_flip() +
    ylim(smd_limits[1], smd_limits[2]) +  # Added ylim parameter for x-axis range
    labs(
      title = paste(title_prefix, "Continuous/Binary Variables"),
      subtitle = "Standardized Mean Differences (SMD) Between Training and Test Sets",
      x = "Variables",
      y = "Standardized Mean Difference",
      color = "Balance Quality",
      shape = "Variable Type",
      caption = "SMD closer to zero = better balance\nThresholds: |SMD| <= 0.05 (excellent), <= 0.1 (good)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )

  # PLOT 2: CATEGORICAL VARIABLES (using Cramer's V)
  categorical_df = map_dfr(categorical_results, function(cat_result) {
    tibble(
      variable = cat_result$variable,
      cramers_v = cat_result$cramers_v,
      n_levels = cat_result$n_levels,
      chi_p_value = cat_result$chi_p_value
    )
  }) %>%
    mutate(
      balance_quality = case_when(
        cramers_v <= 0.05 ~ "Excellent (<=0.05)",
        cramers_v <= 0.1 ~ "Good (0.05-0.1)",
        TRUE ~ "Moderate (>0.1)"
      ),
      balance_quality = factor(balance_quality,
                               levels = c("Excellent (<=0.05)", "Good (0.05-0.1)",
                                          "Moderate (>0.1)"))
    )

  max_cramers = max(categorical_df$cramers_v, na.rm = TRUE)
  y_upper_limit = max(max_cramers * 1.1, 0.25)  # Ensure at least 0.25 to show 0.2 reference line

  categorical_plot = ggplot(categorical_df, aes(x = factor(variable, levels = rev(all_vars_alphabetical)), y = cramers_v)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2),
               color = c("black", "darkgreen", "orange", "red"),
               linetype = c("solid", "dashed", "dashed", "dashed"),
               alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_point(aes(color = balance_quality, size = n_levels), alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Excellent (<=0.05)" = "#006400",
                                  "Good (0.05-0.1)" = "#2E8B57",
                                  "Moderate (>0.1)" = "#FF8C00")) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 4), name = "# Categories") +
    coord_flip() +
    ylim(0, y_upper_limit) +
    labs(
      title = paste(title_prefix, "Categorical Variables"),
      subtitle = "Cramer's V Association Strength Between Training and Test Sets",
      x = "Variables",
      y = "Cramer's V (Association Strength)",
      color = "Balance Quality",
      size = "# Categories",
      caption = "Cramer's V closer to zero = better balance\nMeasures how differently categories are distributed between train/test groups"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )

  return(list(continuous_plot = continuous_plot, categorical_plot = categorical_plot))
}


#' Create combined balance plot showing pre vs post rerandomization
#'
#' @param balance_results_pre Pre-rerandomization balance results
#' @param balance_results_post Post-rerandomization balance results
#' @param categorical_results_pre Pre-rerandomization categorical results
#' @param categorical_results_post Post-rerandomization categorical results
#' @param smd_limits Numeric vector of length 2 specifying y-axis limits for SMD plot. Default c(-0.1, 0.1)
#' @return List containing two ggplot objects: continuous_comparison and categorical_comparison
create_combined_balance_plots = function(balance_results_pre, balance_results_post,
                                         categorical_results_pre, categorical_results_post,
                                         smd_limits = c(-0.1, 0.1)) {

  # PLOT 1: COMBINED CONTINUOUS/BINARY VARIABLES (Pre = Purple, Post = Green)
  continuous_pre = balance_results_pre %>%
    filter(type %in% c("continuous", "binary")) %>%
    select(variable, smd) %>%
    mutate(
      timepoint = "Pre-Rerandomization",
      variable_type = case_when(
        variable %in% c("sex", "birthplace") ~ "Binary",
        TRUE ~ "Continuous"
      )
    )

  continuous_post = balance_results_post %>%
    filter(type %in% c("continuous", "binary")) %>%
    select(variable, smd) %>%
    mutate(
      timepoint = "Post-Rerandomization",
      variable_type = case_when(
        variable %in% c("sex", "birthplace") ~ "Binary",
        TRUE ~ "Continuous"
      )
    )

  continuous_combined = bind_rows(continuous_pre, continuous_post) %>%
    mutate(
      abs_smd = abs(smd),
      balance_quality = case_when(
        abs_smd <= 0.05 ~ "Excellent (<=0.05)",
        abs_smd <= 0.1 ~ "Good (0.05-0.1)",
        TRUE ~ "Moderate (>0.1)"
      ),
      balance_quality = factor(balance_quality,
                               levels = c("Excellent (<=0.05)", "Good (0.05-0.1)",
                                          "Moderate (>0.1)"))
    )

  continuous_comparison = ggplot(continuous_combined, aes(x = factor(variable, levels = rev(all_vars_alphabetical)), y = smd)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-0.2, -0.1, -0.05, 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2),
               color = c("red", "orange", "darkgreen", "black", "darkgreen", "orange", "red"),
               linetype = c("dashed", "dashed", "dashed", "solid", "dashed", "dashed", "dashed"),
               alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_point(aes(color = timepoint, shape = variable_type), size = 3, alpha = 0.8,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Pre-Rerandomization" = "#9370DB",  # Purple
                                  "Post-Rerandomization" = "#228B22"), # Green
                       name = "Timepoint") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("Continuous" = 16, "Binary" = 17), name = "Variable Type") +
    coord_flip() +
    ylim(smd_limits[1], smd_limits[2]) +
    labs(
      title = "Balance Comparison: Pre vs Post Rerandomization (Continuous/Binary Variables)",
      subtitle = "Standardized Mean Differences (SMD) Between Training and Test Sets",
      x = "Variables",
      y = "Standardized Mean Difference",
      color = "Timepoint",
      shape = "Variable Type",
      caption = "Purple = Pre-Rerandomization, Green = Post-Rerandomization\nSMD closer to zero = better balance"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    ) +
    guides(
      color = guide_legend(title = "Timepoint", override.aes = list(size = 4)),
      shape = guide_legend(title = "Variable Type", override.aes = list(size = 4))
    )

  # PLOT 2: COMBINED CATEGORICAL VARIABLES (Pre = Purple, Post = Green)
  categorical_pre_df = map_dfr(categorical_results_pre, function(cat_result) {
    tibble(
      variable = cat_result$variable,
      cramers_v = cat_result$cramers_v,
      n_levels = cat_result$n_levels,
      chi_p_value = cat_result$chi_p_value,
      timepoint = "Pre-Rerandomization"
    )
  })

  categorical_post_df = map_dfr(categorical_results_post, function(cat_result) {
    tibble(
      variable = cat_result$variable,
      cramers_v = cat_result$cramers_v,
      n_levels = cat_result$n_levels,
      chi_p_value = cat_result$chi_p_value,
      timepoint = "Post-Rerandomization"
    )
  })

  categorical_combined_df = bind_rows(categorical_pre_df, categorical_post_df) %>%
    mutate(
      balance_quality = case_when(
        cramers_v <= 0.05 ~ "Excellent (<=0.05)",
        cramers_v <= 0.1 ~ "Good (0.05-0.1)",
        TRUE ~ "Moderate (>0.1)"
      ),
      balance_quality = factor(balance_quality,
                               levels = c("Excellent (<=0.05)", "Good (0.05-0.1)",
                                          "Moderate (>0.1)"))
    )

  max_cramers_combined = max(categorical_combined_df$cramers_v, na.rm = TRUE)
  y_upper_limit_combined = max(max_cramers_combined * 1.1, 0.25)

  categorical_comparison = ggplot(categorical_combined_df, aes(x = factor(variable, levels = rev(all_vars_alphabetical)), y = cramers_v)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2),
               color = c("black", "darkgreen", "orange", "red"),
               linetype = c("solid", "dashed", "dashed", "dashed"),
               alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_point(aes(color = timepoint, size = n_levels), alpha = 0.8,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Pre-Rerandomization" = "#9370DB",  # Purple
                                  "Post-Rerandomization" = "#228B22"), # Green
                       name = "Timepoint") +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 4), name = "# Categories") +
    coord_flip() +
    ylim(0, y_upper_limit_combined) +
    labs(
      title = "Balance Comparison: Pre vs Post Rerandomization (Categorical Variables)",
      subtitle = "Cramer's V Association Strength Between Training and Test Sets",
      x = "Variables",
      y = "Cramer's V (Association Strength)",
      color = "Timepoint",
      size = "# Categories",
      caption = "Purple = Pre-Rerandomization, Green = Post-Rerandomization\nCramer's V closer to zero = better balance"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    ) +
    guides(
      color = guide_legend(title = "Timepoint", override.aes = list(size = 4)),
      size = guide_legend(title = "# Categories", override.aes = list(color = "black"))
    )

  return(list(continuous_comparison = continuous_comparison, categorical_comparison = categorical_comparison))
}
```

# Comparing rerandomization with manual train/test split and tidymodels approach

```{r}
# Compare our rerandomization result with standard tidymodels approach
set.seed(rerand_results$best_split$seed)  # Use same seed as best rerandomization for fair comparison
data_split_tidymodels = initial_split(cope_auo_full, prop = 0.50, strata = "strata_var", pool = 0.05)
train_data_tidymodels = training(data_split_tidymodels)
test_data_tidymodels = testing(data_split_tidymodels)

# Calculate AUC for both methods to compare balance quality
rerandomization_auc = calculate_balance_auc(train_data, test_data, existing_covariates)
tidymodels_auc = calculate_balance_auc(train_data_tidymodels, test_data_tidymodels, existing_covariates)

cat("\n=== METHOD COMPARISON ===\n")
cat("Rerandomization Method - Training:", nrow(train_data), "Testing:", nrow(test_data), "AUC:", round(rerandomization_auc$auc, 4), "\n")
cat("Tidymodels Method - Training:", nrow(train_data_tidymodels), "Testing:", nrow(test_data_tidymodels), "AUC:", round(tidymodels_auc$auc, 4), "\n")

if(rerandomization_auc$auc < tidymodels_auc$auc) {
  cat("\u2713 Rerandomization achieved better balance (lower AUC = better balance)\n")
  improvement_pct = round((tidymodels_auc$auc - rerandomization_auc$auc) / tidymodels_auc$auc * 100, 1)
  cat("  Balance improvement:", improvement_pct, "%\n")
} else {
  cat("! Tidymodels achieved better balance\n")
}
```

# Policy impact regression

```{r}
# Policy Impact Regression Function with Covariates
policy_impact_regression = function(dataset, dataset_name = "Dataset", cluster_var = "RegionName", robust = TRUE) {
  
  # Load required packages
  require(sandwich)
  require(lmtest)
  
  # Print analysis info
  cat(paste("Running analysis for:", dataset_name, "\n"))
  cat(paste("Sample size:", nrow(dataset), "\n\n"))
  
  # Define covariates (excluding outcome and policy variables)
  covariates = c(
    "age_2020", "home", "maritalstatus", "race", "education", "employment", 
    "insurance", "anxiety_disorder_before_covid_lifetime", "anxiety_disorder_1yr_before_covid", 
    "sex", "birthplace", "generalized_anxiety_disorder_before_covid_lifetime",
    "generalized_anxiety_disorder_1yr_before_covid"
  )
  
  # Check if all covariates exist
  missing_covariates = setdiff(covariates, names(dataset))
  if(length(missing_covariates) > 0) {
    warning(paste("The following covariates are missing:", paste(missing_covariates, collapse = ", ")))
    covariates = intersect(covariates, names(dataset))
  }
  
  # Check if clustering variable exists
  if(robust && !is.null(cluster_var) && !(cluster_var %in% names(dataset))) {
    warning(paste("Clustering variable", cluster_var, "not found. Using robust standard errors without clustering."))
    cluster_var = NULL
  }
  
  # Get all policy columns using regex pattern matching
  policy_cols = names(dataset)[grepl("^C[1-7]M_\\d{8}_\\d+d$", names(dataset))]
  
  if(length(policy_cols) == 0) {
    # Print first few column names for debugging
    print("No policy columns found. Sample column names:")
    print(head(names(cope_auo_full), 20))
    stop("No policy columns found. Check column name format.")
  }
  
  # Initialize results storage
  results = tibble()
  heatmap_data = tibble()
  
  # Create progress bar for monitoring
  pb = txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = length(policy_cols), style = 3)
  
  # Analyze each policy window column
  for (i in seq_along(policy_cols)) {
    setTxtProgressBar(pb, i)
    policy_col = policy_cols[i]
    
    # Extract window metadata from column name
    meta = str_match(policy_col, "^C[1-7]M_(\\d{8})_(\\d+)d$")
    
    # Add error checking
    if(is.na(meta[1,1])) {
      warning(paste("Could not extract metadata from column name:", policy_col))
      next
    }
    
    start_date = as.Date(meta[1,2], "%Y%m%d")
    duration = as.numeric(meta[1,3])
    policy = str_extract(policy_col, "^C[1-7]M")
    
    # Construct regression formula
    formula = reformulate(
      termlabels = c(policy_col, covariates),
      response = "gad_score_july"
    )
    
    # Run weighted regression
    model = lm(
      formula,
      data = dataset,
      weights = observation_wt_trim
    )
    
    # Variables to store regression statistics
    policy_estimate = NA
    policy_t_stat = NA
    policy_p_value = NA
    
    # Compute robust or clustered standard errors
    if (robust) {
      if (!is.null(cluster_var)) {
        # Clustered standard errors
        vcov_matrix = vcovCL(model, cluster = dataset[[cluster_var]])
      } else {
        # Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors (HC3)
        vcov_matrix = vcovHC(model, type = "HC3")
      }
      
      # Get the robust coefficient table
      coef_table = coeftest(model, vcov = vcov_matrix)
      
      # Extract policy statistics using the robust standard errors
      policy_index = which(rownames(coef_table) == policy_col)
      
      if (length(policy_index) > 0) {
        policy_estimate = coef_table[policy_index, 1]
        policy_std_error = coef_table[policy_index, 2]
        policy_t_stat = coef_table[policy_index, 3]
        policy_p_value = coef_table[policy_index, 4]
      } else {
        warning(paste("Could not find policy column in model results:", policy_col))
        next
      }
    } else {
      # Use regular standard errors from the model
      tidy_model = broom::tidy(model)
      policy_stats = tidy_model %>% 
        filter(term == policy_col)
      
      if (nrow(policy_stats) == 0) {
        warning(paste("Could not find policy column in model results:", policy_col))
        next
      }
      
      policy_estimate = policy_stats$estimate
      policy_t_stat = policy_stats$statistic
      policy_p_value = policy_stats$p.value
    }
    
    # Store results
    results = bind_rows(results, tibble(
      start_date = start_date,
      duration = duration,
      policy = policy,
      estimate = policy_estimate,
      t_stat = abs(policy_t_stat),
      p_value = policy_p_value,
      dataset = dataset_name  
    ))
  }
  
  close(pb)  # Close progress bar
  
  # Generate FDR-corrected p-values
  results = results %>%
    group_by(policy) %>%
    mutate(fdr_p_value = p.adjust(p_value, method = "fdr")) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Create heatmap data (mean absolute t-statistics)
  heatmap_data = results %>%
    group_by(start_date, duration) %>%
    summarize(mean_abs_t_stat = mean(t_stat, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(dataset = dataset_name)  
  
  # Identify significant results
  significant_uncorrected = results %>%
    filter(p_value <= 0.05) %>%
    group_by(start_date, duration, policy) %>%
    summarize(n_significant = n(), .groups = "drop")
  
  significant_fdr = results %>%
    filter(fdr_p_value <= 0.05) %>%
    group_by(start_date, duration, policy) %>%
    summarize(n_significant = n(), .groups = "drop")
  
  list(
    full_results = results,
    heatmap_data = heatmap_data,
    significant_uncorrected = significant_uncorrected,
    significant_fdr = significant_fdr,
    robust = robust,
    cluster_var = cluster_var,
    dataset_name = dataset_name  
  )
}
```

# T stat sum stats

```{r}

#### T-STAT SUM STATS

# Function to compute descriptive statistics for t-statistics
compute_tstat_descriptives = function(data, variable = "t_stat") {
  # Remove any missing values
  values = data[[variable]][!is.na(data[[variable]])]
  
  # Compute descriptive statistics
  stats = c(
    Min = min(values),
    Q1 = quantile(values, 0.25),
    Median = median(values),
    Mean = mean(values),
    SD = sd(values),
    Q3 = quantile(values, 0.75),
    Max = max(values)
  )
  
  return(round(stats, 3))
}

# Function to create comprehensive descriptive statistics table
create_descriptive_table = function(regression_results, policy_descriptions) {
  # Extract full results and dataset name
  full_results = regression_results$full_results
  dataset_name = regression_results$dataset_name
  
  # Initialize results data frame
  results_df = data.frame()
  
  # Get unique policies from the data
  unique_policies = unique(full_results$policy)
  
  # Compute statistics for each individual policy
  for(policy in unique_policies) {
    policy_data = full_results[full_results$policy == policy, ]
    policy_stats = compute_tstat_descriptives(policy_data)
    policy_row = data.frame(
      Dataset = dataset_name,
      Policy = policy_descriptions[policy],
      t(policy_stats)
    )
    results_df = rbind(results_df, policy_row)
  }
  
  # Compute overall statistics across all policies
  overall_stats = compute_tstat_descriptives(regression_results$heatmap_data, "mean_abs_t_stat")
  overall_row = data.frame(
    Dataset = dataset_name,
    Policy = "Overall (All Policies)",
    t(overall_stats)
  )
  results_df = rbind(results_df, overall_row)
  
  return(results_df)
}

# Function to display formatted descriptive statistics
display_descriptive_stats = function(descriptive_table) {
  cat("T-statistic descriptive statistics\n")
  cat("=====================================\n")
  
  # Split by dataset for organized display
  datasets = unique(descriptive_table$Dataset)
  
  for(dataset in datasets) {
    cat("Dataset:", dataset, "\n")
    cat(paste(rep("-", nchar(dataset) + 9), collapse = ""), "\n")
    
    dataset_data = descriptive_table[descriptive_table$Dataset == dataset, ]
    
    # Create formatted output
    for(i in 1:nrow(dataset_data)) {
      policy_name = dataset_data$Policy[i]
      stats = dataset_data[i, 3:9]  # Skip Dataset and Policy columns
      
      cat(sprintf("%-35s", policy_name))
      cat(sprintf(" Min: %6.3f", stats$Min))
      cat(sprintf(" Q1: %6.3f", stats$Q1))
      cat(sprintf(" Median: %6.3f", stats$Median))
      cat(sprintf(" Mean: %6.3f", stats$Mean))
      cat(sprintf(" (SD: %6.3f)", stats$SD))
      cat(sprintf(" Q3: %6.3f", stats$Q3))
      cat(sprintf(" Max: %6.3f", stats$Max))
      cat("\n")
    }
    cat("\n")
  }
}

# Define policy descriptions mapping
policy_descriptions = c(
  "C1M" = "school_closing",
  "C2M" = "workplace_closing", 
  "C3M" = "cancel_public_events",
  "C4M" = "restrictions_on_gatherings",
  "C5M" = "close_public_transport",
  "C6M" = "stay_at_home_policies",
  "C7M" = "internal_travel_limits"
)

# Generate descriptive statistics for all datasets
cat("=== COMPUTING T-STATISTIC DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS ===\n")

# Compute descriptive statistics for each dataset (post-rerandomization)
descriptives_full = create_descriptive_table(results_full, policy_descriptions)
descriptives_train_post_rand = create_descriptive_table(results_train_post_rand, policy_descriptions)
descriptives_test_post_rand = create_descriptive_table(results_test_post_rand, policy_descriptions)

# Compute descriptive statistics for each dataset (pre-rerandomization)
descriptives_train_pre_rand = create_descriptive_table(results_train_pre_rand, policy_descriptions)
descriptives_test_pre_rand = create_descriptive_table(results_test_pre_rand, policy_descriptions)

# Combine all descriptive statistics
all_descriptives_post_rand = rbind(descriptives_full, descriptives_train_post_rand, descriptives_test_post_rand)
all_descriptives_pre_rand = rbind(descriptives_full, descriptives_train_pre_rand, descriptives_test_pre_rand)

# Display the sum/descriptive stats
display_descriptive_stats(all_descriptives_post_rand)
display_descriptive_stats(all_descriptives_pre_rand)
```

```{r}
# Function to check mean t-statistic ranges across datasets
check_mean_tstat_ranges = function(results_full, results_train, results_test) {
  
  full_range = range(results_full$heatmap_data$mean_abs_t_stat, na.rm = TRUE)
  train_range = range(results_train$heatmap_data$mean_abs_t_stat, na.rm = TRUE)  
  test_range = range(results_test$heatmap_data$mean_abs_t_stat, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  cat("Mean absolute t-statistic ranges by dataset:\n")
  cat("Full Sample: ", round(full_range[1], 2), "-", round(full_range[2], 2), "\n")
  cat("Training Set:", round(train_range[1], 2), "-", round(train_range[2], 2), "\n")
  cat("Testing Set: ", round(test_range[1], 2), "-", round(test_range[2], 2), "\n\n")
  
  global_max = max(c(full_range[2], train_range[2], test_range[2]), na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("Recommended consistent scale: 0 to", round(global_max, 2), "\n")
  
  return(global_max)
}

# Function to create t-statistic heatmap with optional cell highlighting
create_tstat_heatmap = function(heatmap_data, dataset_name = "Dataset", max_mean_t_stat = NULL,
                                highlight_start_date = NULL, highlight_duration = NULL,
                                highlight_color = "white", highlight_linewidth = 1.5) {
  # Ensure start_date is in Date format
  heatmap_data$start_date = as.Date(heatmap_data$start_date)
  
  # Use provided max_mean_t_stat or calculate from data
  if(is.null(max_mean_t_stat)) {
    max_mean_t_stat = max(heatmap_data$mean_abs_t_stat, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Base plot
  p = ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = start_date, y = duration, fill = mean_abs_t_stat)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient(
      low = "white", 
      high = "red",
      breaks = seq(0, max_mean_t_stat, by = 0.50),  
      limits = c(0, max_mean_t_stat)  
    ) +
    scale_x_date(
      breaks = seq(
        from = as.Date("2020-03-15"),
        to = as.Date("2020-06-21"),
        by = "1 week"
      ),
      date_labels = "%b %d",
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = seq(7, max(heatmap_data$duration), by = 7),
      labels = function(x) paste(x, "days")
    ) +
    theme_classic() +  
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold", size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray40", size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title.align = 0.5
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Policy Impact Heatmap -", dataset_name),
      subtitle = "Mean Absolute t-statistics for COVID Policy Effects on July Anxiety Scores",
      x = "Exposure Window Start Date",
      y = "Exposure Duration",
      fill = "Mean\n|Absolute t-statistic|",
      caption = "Adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical covariates\nWeighted by inverse probability weights\nRobust standard errors clustered by region"
    )
  
  # Add highlight outline if specified
  if(!is.null(highlight_start_date) && !is.null(highlight_duration)) {
    highlight_date = as.Date(highlight_start_date)
    
    # Calculate tile boundaries (tiles are 7 days wide on both axes)
    p = p + geom_rect(
      xmin = highlight_date - 3.5,
      xmax = highlight_date + 3.5,
      ymin = highlight_duration - 3.5,
      ymax = highlight_duration + 3.5,
      fill = NA,
      color = highlight_color,
      linewidth = highlight_linewidth
    )
  }
  
  return(p)
}
```

# Generate SD Heatmaps

```{r}
# Function to compute SD of t-statistics across policies for each window
compute_sd_heatmap_data = function(full_results, dataset_name = "Dataset") {
  sd_data = full_results %>%
    group_by(start_date, duration) %>%
    summarize(sd_abs_t_stat = sd(t_stat, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(dataset = dataset_name)
  
  return(sd_data)
}

# Function to create SD t-statistic heatmap
create_sd_tstat_heatmap = function(sd_heatmap_data, dataset_name = "Dataset", max_sd_t_stat = NULL,
                                   highlight_start_date = NULL, highlight_duration = NULL,
                                   highlight_color = "white", highlight_linewidth = 1.5) {
  # Ensure start_date is in Date format
  sd_heatmap_data$start_date = as.Date(sd_heatmap_data$start_date)
  
  # Use provided max_sd_t_stat or calculate from data
  if(is.null(max_sd_t_stat)) {
    max_sd_t_stat = max(sd_heatmap_data$sd_abs_t_stat, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Base plot
  p = ggplot(sd_heatmap_data, aes(x = start_date, y = duration, fill = sd_abs_t_stat)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient(
      low = "white", 
      high = "#3333FF",
      breaks = seq(0, max_sd_t_stat, by = 0.50),  
      limits = c(0, max_sd_t_stat)  
    ) +
    scale_x_date(
      breaks = seq(
        from = as.Date("2020-03-15"),
        to = as.Date("2020-06-21"),
        by = "1 week"
      ),
      date_labels = "%b %d",
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = seq(7, max(sd_heatmap_data$duration), by = 7),
      labels = function(x) paste(x, "days")
    ) +
    theme_classic() +  
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray40", size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title.align = 0.5
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Policy Variability Heatmap -", dataset_name),
      subtitle = "Standard Deviation of Absolute t-statistics Across Policies Within Each Window",
      x = "Exposure Window Start Date",
      y = "Exposure Duration",
      fill = "SD\n|Absolute t-statistic|",
      caption = "Adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical covariates\nWeighted by inverse probability weights\nRobust standard errors clustered by region"
    )
  
  # Add highlight outline if specified
  if(!is.null(highlight_start_date) && !is.null(highlight_duration)) {
    highlight_date = as.Date(highlight_start_date)
    
    p = p + geom_rect(
      xmin = highlight_date - 3.5,
      xmax = highlight_date + 3.5,
      ymin = highlight_duration - 3.5,
      ymax = highlight_duration + 3.5,
      fill = NA,
      color = highlight_color,
      linewidth = highlight_linewidth
    )
  }
  
  return(p)
}

#----------------------------------------------------
# Individual exposure policy heatmaps
#----------------------------------------------------
# First, create policy-specific heatmap data frames
create_individual_policy_heatmap_data = function(regression_results) {
  # Extract policy prefixes from full results
  policy_prefixes = unique(regression_results$full_results$policy)
  
  # Create list to store policy-specific heatmaps
  individual_policy_data = list()
  
  # For each policy, create a specific heatmap dataset
  for(prefix in policy_prefixes) {
    # Filter results for this policy
    policy_results = regression_results$full_results %>%
      filter(policy == prefix)
    
    # Create heatmap data (using t_stat directly)
    individual_policy_data[[prefix]] = policy_results %>%
      select(start_date, duration, t_stat) %>%
      # Ensure data is properly sorted
      arrange(start_date, duration)
  }
  
  return(individual_policy_data)
}

# Create a function to generate consistent heatmaps for each policy
create_policy_heatmap = function(data, policy_name, policy_description, dataset_name = "", max_t_stat = NULL) {
  # Check if data contains t_stat column
  if(!"t_stat" %in% names(data)) {
    stop("Policy heatmap data must contain 't_stat' column")
  }
  
  # Ensure start_date is in Date format
  data$start_date = as.Date(data$start_date)
  
  # Use provided max_t_stat or calculate from data
  if(is.null(max_t_stat)) {
    max_t_stat = max(data$t_stat, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Add dataset name to title if provided
  title_text = if(dataset_name != "") {
    paste("Policy Impact Heatmap:", policy_description, "-", dataset_name)
  } else {
    paste("Policy Impact Heatmap:", policy_description)
  }
  
  ggplot(data, aes(x = start_date, y = duration, fill = t_stat)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient(
      low = "white", 
      high = "red",
      breaks = seq(0, max_t_stat, by = 0.5),
      limits = c(0, max_t_stat)  # Force consistent limits
    ) +
    scale_x_date(
      breaks = seq(
        from = as.Date("2020-03-15"),
        to = as.Date("2020-06-21"),
        by = "1 week"
      ),
      date_labels = "%b %d",
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = seq(7, max(data$duration), by = 7),
      labels = function(x) paste(x, "days")
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray40", size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
      legend.position = "right"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = title_text,
      subtitle = "Absolute t-statistics for Policy Effects on July Anxiety",
      x = "Exposure Window Start Date",
      y = "Exposure Duration",
      fill = "|Absolute t-statistic|",  
      caption = "Adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical covariates\nWeighted by inverse probability weights\nRobust standard errors clustered by region"
    )
}

  "C4M" = "Restrictions on Gatherings (C4M)",

  full_sample = results_full,
  training_set = results_train_post_rand,
  testing_set = results_test_post_rand

# Store results for organized access and individual policy analysis (pre-randomization)
analysis_results_pre_rand = list(
  full_sample = results_full,  # Full sample stays the same
  training_set = results_train_pre_rand,
  testing_set = results_test_pre_rand
)

# Function to calculate policy-specific maximum t-statistics across all datasets and randomization statuses
calculate_policy_specific_scales = function() {
  
  policy_max_scales = list()
  
  for(policy in names(policy_descriptions)) {
    
    cat("Calculating consistent scale for policy:", policy, "\n")
    
    # Collect all t-statistics for this policy across all datasets and randomization statuses
    all_t_stats_for_policy = c()
    
    # POST-RANDOMIZATION DATA
    if(policy %in% names(individual_policy_full_post_rand)) {
      all_t_stats_for_policy = c(all_t_stats_for_policy, individual_policy_full_post_rand[[policy]]$t_stat)
    }
    if(policy %in% names(individual_policy_train_post_rand)) {
      all_t_stats_for_policy = c(all_t_stats_for_policy, individual_policy_train_post_rand[[policy]]$t_stat)
    }
    if(policy %in% names(individual_policy_test_post_rand)) {
      all_t_stats_for_policy = c(all_t_stats_for_policy, individual_policy_test_post_rand[[policy]]$t_stat)
    }
    
    # PRE-RANDOMIZATION DATA
    if(policy %in% names(individual_policy_full_pre_rand)) {
      all_t_stats_for_policy = c(all_t_stats_for_policy, individual_policy_full_pre_rand[[policy]]$t_stat)
    }
    if(policy %in% names(individual_policy_train_pre_rand)) {
      all_t_stats_for_policy = c(all_t_stats_for_policy, individual_policy_train_pre_rand[[policy]]$t_stat)
    }
    if(policy %in% names(individual_policy_test_pre_rand)) {
      all_t_stats_for_policy = c(all_t_stats_for_policy, individual_policy_test_pre_rand[[policy]]$t_stat)
    }
    
    # Calculate the maximum for this policy
    policy_max_scales[[policy]] = max(all_t_stats_for_policy, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    cat("  Policy", policy, "consistent scale: 0 to", round(policy_max_scales[[policy]], 2), "\n")
  }
  
  return(policy_max_scales)
}
```

# Final Comparisons

```{r}
# Function to display policy comparison across datasets
show_policy_comparison = function(policy_name, comparison_type = "post_rand", save_pdf = TRUE, filename = NULL) {
  
  if(!(policy_name %in% names(policy_descriptions))) {
    cat("Policy not found. Available policies:", paste(names(policy_descriptions), collapse = ", "), "\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Use correct variable names for pre_rand and post_rand
  if(comparison_type == "post_rand") {
    # Post-rerandomization comparison - use post_rand data
    policy_data_full = individual_policy_full_post_rand
    policy_data_train = individual_policy_train_post_rand
    policy_data_test = individual_policy_test_post_rand
    subtitle_suffix = "(Post-Rerandomization)"
    
    # Calculate max_t_stats ONLY from post-rerandomization data
    max_t_stats_post = c()
    if(policy_name %in% names(policy_data_full)) {
      max_t_stats_post = c(max_t_stats_post, max(policy_data_full[[policy_name]]$t_stat, na.rm = TRUE))
    }
    if(policy_name %in% names(policy_data_train)) {
      max_t_stats_post = c(max_t_stats_post, max(policy_data_train[[policy_name]]$t_stat, na.rm = TRUE))
    }
    if(policy_name %in% names(policy_data_test)) {
      max_t_stats_post = c(max_t_stats_post, max(policy_data_test[[policy_name]]$t_stat, na.rm = TRUE))
    }
    overall_max = max(max_t_stats_post, na.rm = TRUE)
    
  } else if(comparison_type == "pre_rand") {
    # Pre-rerandomization comparison - use pre_rand data
    policy_data_full = policy_data_full_pre_rand
    policy_data_train = policy_data_train_pre_rand
    policy_data_test = policy_data_test_pre_rand
    subtitle_suffix = "(Pre-Rerandomization)"
    
    # Calculate max_t_stats ONLY from pre-rerandomization data
    max_t_stats_pre = c()
    if(policy_name %in% names(policy_data_full)) {
      max_t_stats_pre = c(max_t_stats_pre, max(policy_data_full[[policy_name]]$t_stat, na.rm = TRUE))
    }
    if(policy_name %in% names(policy_data_train)) {
      max_t_stats_pre = c(max_t_stats_pre, max(policy_data_train[[policy_name]]$t_stat, na.rm = TRUE))
    }
    if(policy_name %in% names(policy_data_test)) {
      max_t_stats_pre = c(max_t_stats_pre, max(policy_data_test[[policy_name]]$t_stat, na.rm = TRUE))
    }
    overall_max = max(max_t_stats_pre, na.rm = TRUE)
    
  } else {
    cat("Invalid comparison_type. Use 'post_rand' or 'pre_rand'\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  cat("Using consistent t-statistic scale for", comparison_type, ": 0 to", round(overall_max, 2), "\n")
  
  # Step 2: Recreate plots with consistent scale
  plot_full = create_policy_heatmap(
    policy_data_full[[policy_name]], 
    policy_name, 
    policy_descriptions[policy_name], 
    paste("Full Sample", subtitle_suffix),
    max_t_stat = overall_max
  )
  
  plot_train = create_policy_heatmap(
    policy_data_train[[policy_name]], 
    policy_name, 
    policy_descriptions[policy_name], 
    paste("Training Set", subtitle_suffix),
    max_t_stat = overall_max
  )
  
  plot_test = create_policy_heatmap(
    policy_data_test[[policy_name]], 
    policy_name, 
    policy_descriptions[policy_name], 
    paste("Testing Set", subtitle_suffix),
    max_t_stat = overall_max
  )
  
  # Step 3: Create the combined plot
  combined_plot = grid.arrange(
    plot_full, plot_train, plot_test,
    ncol = 3,
    top = textGrob(paste(policy_descriptions[policy_name], "- Dataset Comparison", subtitle_suffix),
                   gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold"))
  )
  
  if(save_pdf) {
    # Generate filename if not provided
    if(is.null(filename)) {
      filename = paste0("policy_comparison_", policy_name, "_", comparison_type, "_updated.pdf")
    }
    
    # Save as PDF
    ggsave(
      filename = filename,
      plot = combined_plot,
      width = 30, 
      height = 8,   
      device = "pdf"
    )
    
    cat("Policy comparison saved as:", filename, "\n")
    
    # Display the PDF
    file.show(filename)
  }
  
  return(combined_plot)
}

# Updated to include logic for pre and post rand
show_all_policies_dataset = function(dataset_name, comparison_type = "post_rand", save_pdf = TRUE, filename = NULL) {
  
  # Check valid inputs
  if(!(dataset_name %in% c("full_sample", "training_set", "testing_set"))) {
    cat("Dataset not found. Available datasets: full_sample, training_set, testing_set\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  if(!(comparison_type %in% c("post_rand", "pre_rand"))) {
    cat("Invalid comparison_type. Use 'post_rand' or 'pre_rand'\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Select the appropriate policy data based on comparison_type
  if(comparison_type == "post_rand") {
    dataset_policy_data = switch(dataset_name,
                                 "full_sample" = individual_policy_full_post_rand,
                                 "training_set" = individual_policy_train_post_rand,
                                 "testing_set" = individual_policy_test_post_rand
    )
    subtitle_suffix = "(Post-Rerandomization)"
  } else if(comparison_type == "pre_rand") {
    dataset_policy_data = switch(dataset_name,
                                 "full_sample" = individual_policy_full_pre_rand,
                                 "training_set" = individual_policy_train_pre_rand,
                                 "testing_set" = individual_policy_test_pre_rand
    )
    subtitle_suffix = "(Pre-Rerandomization)"
  }
  
  # Find the maximum t-statistic across all policies for this dataset
  all_t_stats = c()
  for(policy in names(dataset_policy_data)) {
    all_t_stats = c(all_t_stats, dataset_policy_data[[policy]]$t_stat)
  }
  
  overall_max = max(all_t_stats, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  cat("Using consistent t-statistic scale for", dataset_name, comparison_type, ": 0 to", round(overall_max, 2), "\n")
  
  # Recreate plots with consistent scale
  consistent_plots = list()
  for(policy in names(policy_descriptions)) {
    if(policy %in% names(dataset_policy_data)) {
      consistent_plots[[policy]] = create_policy_heatmap(
        dataset_policy_data[[policy]], 
        policy, 
        policy_descriptions[policy], 
        paste(gsub("_", " ", stringr::str_to_title(dataset_name)), subtitle_suffix),
        max_t_stat = overall_max
      )
    }
  }
  
  # Create the combined plot
  combined_plot = grid.arrange(
    grobs = consistent_plots,
    ncol = 3,
    nrow = 3,
    top = textGrob(paste("All Policies -", gsub("_", " ", stringr::str_to_title(dataset_name)), subtitle_suffix),
                   gp = gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold"))
  )
  
  if(save_pdf) {
    # Generate filename if not provided
    if(is.null(filename)) {
      clean_dataset_name = gsub("_", "_", dataset_name)
      filename = paste0("all_policies_", clean_dataset_name, "_", comparison_type, "_updated.pdf")
    }
    
    # Save as PDF
    ggsave(
      filename = filename,
      plot = combined_plot,
      width = 15,  # inches
      height = 12,  # inches  
      device = "pdf"
    )
    
    cat("All policies plot saved as:", filename, "\n")
    
    # Display the PDF
    file.show(filename)
  }
  
  return(combined_plot)
}

# Function to check t-statistic ranges (helpful for verification)
check_tstat_ranges = function(comparison_type = "post_rand") {
  
  if(!(comparison_type %in% c("post_rand", "pre_rand"))) {
    cat("Invalid comparison_type. Use 'post_rand' or 'pre_rand'\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Select appropriate data based on comparison_type
  if(comparison_type == "post_rand") {
    policy_data_full = individual_policy_full_post_rand
    policy_data_train = individual_policy_train_post_rand
    policy_data_test = individual_policy_test_post_rand
    suffix = "(Post-Rerandomization)"
  } else {
    policy_data_full = individual_policy_full_pre_rand
    policy_data_train = individual_policy_train_pre_rand
    policy_data_test = individual_policy_test_pre_rand
    suffix = "(Pre-Rerandomization)"
  }
  
  cat("T-statistic ranges by policy and dataset", suffix, ":\n\n")
  
  for(policy in names(policy_descriptions)) {
    cat("Policy:", policy, "-", policy_descriptions[policy], "\n")
    
    if(policy %in% names(policy_data_full)) {
      full_range = range(policy_data_full[[policy]]$t_stat, na.rm = TRUE)
      cat("  Full Sample: ", round(full_range[1], 2), "-", round(full_range[2], 2), "\n")
    }
    
    if(policy %in% names(policy_data_train)) {
      train_range = range(policy_data_train[[policy]]$t_stat, na.rm = TRUE)
      cat("  Training Set:", round(train_range[1], 2), "-", round(train_range[2], 2), "\n")
    }
    
    if(policy %in% names(policy_data_test)) {
      test_range = range(policy_data_test[[policy]]$t_stat, na.rm = TRUE)
      cat("  Testing Set: ", round(test_range[1], 2), "-", round(test_range[2], 2), "\n")
    }
    
    cat("\n")
  }
}
```
